title: pullAndRefresh() is not nonReentrant and can be re-entered by a malicious or upgradable dispatcherHook
description:
`pullAndRefresh()` is an external, permissionless entry point that calls `_syncBudget`, which in turn calls `dispatcherHook.pull()`. `_syncBudget` performs state mutations AFTER the external call: it measures `inflow` from a balance delta and then updates `rewardBudget`, `windowEnd`, and `rewardRate`. Unlike `stake`/`unstake`/`claim`, `pullAndRefresh` carries no `nonReentrant` modifier. The `dispatcherHook` address is mutable (`setDispatcherHook`) and is documented as a sibling-controlled contract — not an immutable trusted primitive.

A compromised, buggy, or upgraded dispatcher can reenter `pullAndRefresh` (or `stake`/`unstake`/`claim`, but those are guarded) from inside its own `pull()`. During the nested call, `_updatePool` runs against stale `rewardRate` and `windowEnd` values while `pre` is captured mid-transfer, enabling inflow to be counted more than once or the window to be reset against an inconsistent intermediate state. At minimum the invariant `pre + inflow == post` relied upon by the outer frame breaks because the nested frame also mutates `rewardBudget` / `rewardRate`.
impact: If the dispatcher hook is ever malicious or buggy, cross-function reentrancy via the unguarded `pullAndRefresh` can corrupt `rewardBudget`, `rewardRate`, or `windowEnd`. This does not directly steal user stake (nonReentrant-guarded user entrypoints still hold), but it can produce inflated emissions or stuck windows that bleed rewards incorrectly.
proof: Mechanism: (1) attacker-controlled dispatcher is set via `setDispatcherHook` (e.g., post-upgrade); (2) attacker calls `pullAndRefresh`; (3) inside `pull()`, attacker calls `pullAndRefresh` again; (4) nested `_updatePool` runs, nested `pull()` triggers yet another balance inflow against `pre` captured in the nested frame; (5) control returns to the outer frame, which computes `inflow = balance - outer_pre` — but `outer_pre` is stale, the nested frame already consumed part of the delta. The outer frame will add the already-credited inflow again, double-counting it into `rewardBudget`.
recommendation: Add `nonReentrant` to `pullAndRefresh`. Consider adding a reentrancy guard to `_syncBudget` itself, or refactor so `rewardBudget += inflow` is computed from a delta captured atomically (e.g., `dispatcherHook.pull()` returns the minted amount and you add it directly instead of balance-sniffing). Also document and audit the trust level of `dispatcherHook` — treating it as untrusted is the safer stance.
